text:
Matthew Schaefer is 19, the reigning Calder Trophy winner, and already the Islanders' most important skater. He plays 26 minutes and 55 seconds a night, more than two minutes up from his rookie year, and has 26 points in 25 games, a point a game from a defenseman who isn't old enough to drink in the building.

Some of it is running hot. His shooting (10.3%) sits at the top of our range for him, and his pace, 2.32 points per 60, is above what we'd expect him to hold. But the play-driving isn't a mirage: Evolving-Hockey had him 99th percentile among defensemen for pushing expected goals last season, while playing with weaker teammates. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking shows him joining the rush far more than most defensemen.

The last week has been quieter. Stefen Rosner of NHL.com put it plainly: "Schaefer has been human these last five or so games." He has one multi-point game since a hat trick against Columbus on Nov. 17. Off the ice, he's been in the news for honoring his late mother with a cancer support room. Watch whether New York keeps leaning on him for 31 minutes some nights.
